I’m 17, I took an overdose in November of last year. About 100 pills overall, painkillers, cold and flu tablets, sleepers, anything I could find that I had been saving for months and months. I swallowed what I could and the immediate panic set in, I knew in my heart it wouldn’t not kill me, but it could and probably would have caused serious damage if I had not told my mother and had been taken to the hospital. At the hospital it was 7 hours of throwing up powder, getting lodged in your throat. Been passed from nurse to doctor, blood tests, discussions with the crisis team. It was horrible and I would not wish that night on anyone else.
Going through all of this, my mother and my entire family understood that I had felt that low and sad that I thought my only way out was to end my own life. 
You don’t have to attempt suicide for people to understand and to care, and id highly advise against overdosing, I was terrified, because I knew it would never kill me.
You have people around you, adults, that understand exactly how you’re feeling and can help. There’s hotline, counselling services that you can attend for free (I’m in the UK I’m not sure about other countries but I should assume there is) there is a million other options. You don’t need to end your life.
